conclusions: The only firmware source difference from the sealed E3f-9d.2 build is board pclk_hz=20 MHz. PSRAM direct transmission, 4092-byte chunks, queue depth 2, source-buffer ownership, menu repair and first-frame handling remain unchanged.

Independent build verification passes against the retained complete source/dependency inventory; effective configuration, protected build outputs and internal static data (65216 bytes) match the baseline.
The new candidate-only boot gate rejects all eight observed display error markers before normal candidate boot acceptance; the finally block clears candidate checking before same-run restoration.

Production transaction integration tests inject each display error, partial write and failed boot, and verify exact restoration of the original App with NVS and paired resources preserved. The actual E3f-9d.2 failure log is rejected.
The original App recovery remains independent of candidate files and older references; restoration uses same-run bytes and identity checks, while preserving current NVS.
20 MHz is a suitable isolated comparison of instantaneous PSRAM supply pressure. It is not a demonstrated fix until boot logs and real screen/load checks pass.
Current documents accurately state that E3f-9d.2 failed transport validation and E3f-9d.1 was restored; E3f-9d.3 is built and offline-reviewed before installation.
limits: The boot error gate covers the 45-second captured startup log; later Wi-Fi, conversation, menus and two-role switching require separate real-device observation.
Host harness checks pixel contents and queued-buffer lifetime but does not emulate ISR scheduling, actual memory-bus contention or display output.
IDF may keep stale LCD inflight accounting after DMA underflow; any underflow, recycling or blit failure requires a failed result and restoration rather than continuing the same display instance.
Intermittent black screen, USB power-switch behavior and first full-screen initialization remain separate startup validation work.
